basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity and renal disease are defining BBS features; developmental/intellectual impairment in 1/1. Polydactyly omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal disease is a major BBS diagnostic feature; renal insufficiency is reported in 1/1 annotated patient.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay and intellectual disability occur in 1/1; retained alongside the defining retinal, metabolic and renal axes.

basis: Contractures, neurodevelopmental defects and Pierre Robin oral anomalies define the syndrome. OSA is reported in 30-79% but does not establish direct pulmonary damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: OSA (30-79%) is secondary to oral/jaw anatomy and separately diagnosed; no direct lung or airway lesion is established.

basis: The primary defect is the abdominal wall; pulmonary hypoplasia and restrictive dysfunction occur in 30-79%. Herniated bowel alone does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal disease.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the malformation affects the abdominal wall; displacement of otherwise intact bowel does not establish gastrointestinal damage.

basis: Parathyroid malignancy with PTH-mediated bone loss; osteoporosis occurs in 30-79%. Renal insufficiency is 5-29%; stones are separate, and nephrocalcinosis alone does not prove dysfunction.

decisions.renal: none: renal insufficiency is only 5-29%; stones are separately diagnosed, and frequent nephrocalcinosis does not establish functional impairment.

basis: Brain/limb defects define syndrome; cardiac defects and optic atrophy occur in 80-99%. Respiratory insufficiency and microtia (80-99%) omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone is not liver damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital cardiac septal abnormalities and patent ductus arteriosus are reported in 80-99%.
decisions.pulmonary: none under cap: respiratory insufficiency is 80-99%, but definite brain, skeletal, cardiac and optic pathology take priority.
decisions.ocular: involved: optic atrophy is direct, irreversible visual-system damage reported in 80-99%.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines disease; hypothyroidism and structural external-ear hypoplasia each occur in 2/5 (40%). Cardiac defect is 1/5; apnea/reflux do not prove direct organ injury.

decisions.otologic: involved: microtia is structural hypoplasia of the external ear in 2/5 (40%), rather than merely an unusually positioned ear.

basis: Heme synthesis disorders; cutaneous forms, dominated by PCT, comprise over half of clinically manifest cases and cause photosensitive skin injury. Neurologic injury is restricted to acute forms.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous porphyrias, chiefly PCT, comprise >50% of clinically manifest porphyria and directly damage skin; not a minority subtype complication.

basis: Colon is the tumour origin; liver metastases directly occupy hepatic tissue in roughly 60-70% of metastatic colorectal cancers. This is spread of the same disease.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic metastases occur in roughly 60-70% of metastatic colorectal cancer; the unspecified destination does not negate common direct hepatic occupation.

basis: Callosal agenesis/intellectual disability, microphthalmia and heminasal hypoplasia define brain, eye and nasal defects. Unspecified atypical clefting does not establish oral/palatal involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: heminasal hypoplasia is a defining nasal malformation; the nose belongs to the pulmonary axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: the record does not localize atypical clefting to the mouth or palate; a gastrointestinal malformation cannot be assumed.

basis: Mosaic Edwards syndrome has variable neurodevelopmental and characteristic limb defects. Congenital heart defects affect roughly 40% of reported mosaic cases; full-trisomy frequencies are not used.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: congenital heart defects occur in roughly 40% of reported mosaic cases, meeting the threshold despite variable expression.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic hand/foot malformations and contractures are defining Edwards skeletal features, including in its mosaic presentation.
